rules_evaluated.evidence: Shortest chunk: chunk 2 (L25-28), one bullet -- 'The rule that arrives generic, like "pick tasks that span multiple files," is the one to rewrite in your words, or reject.' -- a complete, self-carrying directive with a concrete example, not a wait-state fragment. Every other chunk carries >=2 bullets, a table, or framing prose plus a prompt fence.

Checked all 9 `##` headers against chunk content; each is a literally true summary (e.g. chunk 5 'Where rules can live, and when they load' against the table at L53-59; chunk 9 'Phase 5: Leave the repo tidier than you found it' against the Boy Scout bullets at L104-106). Closest candidate: chunk 9's header promises tidying but content only asks Claude to NAME gaps (maintainer L136: 'Fixing is the student's call... do not add a fix-it prompt') -- not a contradiction, this is the standard Phase-label pattern (names the frame; body explains applying it, L104 'Write it down where the next planner will read it').

Ran targeted greps on the body (L1-111): `grep -nE "\bNot [A-Z]"` -> 0 hits (no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'); `grep -niE "most useful|one of the|best way|game.chang|essential|crucial"` -> 0 hits (no self-grading superlative); numerals present are only widget-chrome time budgets (L3 '20 minutes', L15 '8 min', L41 '4 min', L68 '3 min', L82 '3 min', L100 '2 min') with no retraction/hedge attached, so no number+retraction pattern; no anaphora/epistrophe triple or empty-leg verb triplet found on a manual read of every bullet.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `grep -nE '\*\*[A-Za-z][^*]{0,60}\*\*'` on the body (L1-111) -> bold appears only at widget chrome (L3,5,7,9, exempt) and chunk 9 L104-106: '**Planning gaps.**', '**Conflicting information.**', '**Other context.**' -- three bolded checklist-item-name handles (each within the <=5-word span cap) on ONE slide, against the default <=1-per-slide budget. None of the rule's named exemptions covers it on inspection: not a §34 task-sizing floor/ceiling callout, not a `## What You'll Learn` LO-template bullet, not a scanned menu/reading-list slide (this is a worked taxonomy read top-to-bottom, not an entry-point menu), not a reference/supplementary lookup page (this is an ordinary exercise Phase). The 'law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law' clause is the nearest fit, but these three categories are introduced fresh here rather than consolidating previously-earned named laws, so it is a genuine boundary case rather than a clean exemption. The maintainer's OWN accept-note at L130 states the opposite design intent for this file: '**Emphasis budget (`check_slides.md §9`):** no bolded handles in the body; all bullet leads plain.' -- undated, sitting before the L136 note ('Phase 5 Boy Scout slide (Antti-directed 2026-08-23; moved here 2026-08-25)') that records when these three bullets entered this file, so the accept-note plausibly predates and no longer describes the current body. Harm: the rule exists so bold stays a reliable navigation signal; three short, non-noisy checklist labels are a mild instance of the harm, but the file's own maintainer note explicitly disclaims exactly this pattern for this file, which is the ambiguity a maintainer call should resolve rather than have re-litigated by every future judge.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either drop to one bolded handle (or none) across the three Boy Scout bullets to match the file's own stated 'all bullet leads plain' intent, or add a dated accept-note authorizing the checklist-enumeration bold and refresh L130 so it no longer claims the opposite.
